name: Terraform joining anchors judged by what they reach
summary: Judges Terraform joining anchors per instance across both listed provider rules and unlisted declarations, adds directed Azure joining rules, and stops pure links from inventing self-evidence when an external end is opaque.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/HBlhIeSD#5SMX69gS
changes.value: The checker reads current architecture, one selected state, or independent drafts. It reports bindings, anchors, declared relationships, interfaces, module depth and document references with canonical identities. It reads the interface of every bound module, with or without parts, in every language that the module holds, and hands Module depth what it read. EXPOSED_UNUSED is a warning when the reader resolved every use in that language and the model draws no outside caller of the entry; otherwise it is information. The answer marks the modules that the branch touched and carries the selected model's shallow-module setting; severities in the answer never depend on the caller's flags. Its state reader also reads one selected state at a source ref, through the branch reading, for the branch footprint of a named head. Git locality and branch footprint use separate requested history operations. The timings of its language servers name the program that ran and the TypeScript that it read. An anchor on a Terraform declaration that neither end holds is judged per declaration instance: an unlisted declaration supports the relationship when one instance reaches code held by both claimed ends (or their descendants) without emitting undrawn evidence, and a listed join checks its endpoint roles per instance — supporting a matching pair in either orientation, warning ANCHOR_MISMATCH when every instance resolves both sides to other bound parts, and withholding the warning when an opaque end leaves room for a match. Pure-link declarations never fall back to themselves as an end when an external end is unresolved.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/6E6hL0Zk#3CaBjhIM
changes.value: Module exposure reads every language that a module holds, not only the first one that matches. Each grammar query also names the kind of each export, the pieces of logic in each body, and the expression around each use of a name that another file defines. For Terraform, provider rules name the declarations that join two others: the evidence kind, the arguments for each end, and whether the declaration itself stands for an end that no argument resolves (true for triggers and pull subscriptions, false for pure links). Azure adds directed configured-path rules for subnet NAT gateway associations, diagnostic settings (excluding credential arguments), private DNS zone virtual network links, and NAT gateway public IP associations; undirected NSG filter attachments stay unlisted.
